sentence_of_record: ROUTER-CLEAN-POLICY (2f53675; recomputed independently in this review). On the split of record, the per-cell model policies were fitted on the 15,124 TRAIN questions outside pool paeec37aa28063c75 and scored on all 6,482 EVAL questions in the 52 fixed (source, domain) strata: 18 open-weight leaderboard models, key-scored, MATH-FIX labels. Choosing the TRAIN-best model for the (source, domain) cell PREDICTED by the federated union tree beats the single TRAIN-best model (Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct, 0.5912 → 0.6203) by +2.92pp. The two-stage 95% interval is [+1.81, +4.02]; it re-fits the policy on every replicate (measured DEFF 1.31-1.37, n_eff ≈ 4,700-4,900, MDE 1.6pp). The tree reads that cell from the nearest of 143 leaf centroids, and its depth-1/2 anchors ARE the 52 designed strata. The same policy on the TRUE labels gains +3.09pp [+1.98, +4.19], so the gain is the per-cell model choice over SUPPLIED cells. Reading the cell from the tree instead of the declared label changes accuracy by M = +0.17pp [−0.61, +0.95]. That is not distinguishable from zero at this support (MDE ≈ 1.1pp), and neither a cost nor parity is shown. About two thirds of the gain comes from BBH (+1.96 of +2.92pp), and on the MMLU-Pro source alone it is +0.86pp [−0.54, +2.26]. It survives removing the 478 EVAL questions with a TRAIN text twin (+3.28 [+2.12, +4.44]). It replaces MC-E2E's +3.38pp and +0.71pp, whose policies were fitted partly on reserved questions.

plain_description.what: It re-measured the gain from choosing the best model per cell (cell = benchmark x domain, predicted by the tree), compared with always using the single best model. Policies were fitted only on training questions and scored on all 6,482 held-out questions, with an interval that includes policy-fitting noise.
plain_description.why: The earlier gain (+3.38 points) had been fitted partly on held-out questions, so it needed a clean re-read.
plain_description.information: A clean positive gain supports per-cell routing as useful. No gain would withdraw the claim. Result: done. Per-cell choice beats the single best model by +2.9 points (95% interval +1.8 to +4.0), replacing the old figure. The cells are supplied (declared), not discovered, so this is not evidence that the taxonomy was discovered. About two thirds of the gain comes from BBH, and MMLU-Pro alone shows no clear gain. Reading the cell from the tree instead of the true label changes accuracy by an amount not distinguishable from zero (a cost below about 1 point is neither shown nor excluded).
